name: Aiah
overview: Aiah was a male Edomite, identified in Scripture as the son of Zibeon. His lineage places him within the Edomite tribe, a people descended from Esau. Beyond his paternal relationship, the biblical record provides no additional details about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Aiah means 'black kite,' a proper name recorded in Genesis 36:24. This designation does not appear to have been given by God but reflects a characteristic or symbolic meaning attributed to him in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Aiah was the son of Zibeon. No other family relationships are noted, limiting our understanding of his broader familial connections.
scriptureSignificance: Aiah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical mention within the Edomite lineage, highlighting the descendants of Zibeon. His inclusion in the biblical record serves to trace the ancestry and tribal affiliations important for understanding the historical and ethnic background of the Edomites, who play a role in the broader biblical narrative.
